note: Frozen check list for design-doc evals 7, 71, 9 and 10. Written before any run of iteration-21 and not edited to fit an output. Caveat: its author had already read one with-skill run of each eval (iteration-20) when writing it. Each assertion in evals.json is decomposed into atomic yes/no checks. kind=file and kind=absence are decided by a script from the bytes on disk; kind=reply and kind=invention are decided by an LLM judge in a packet that does not name the arm (one pass for reply, three independent passes for invention, met only when unanimous, a split is borderline and counted as not met). A met reply check quotes the words that satisfy it; an unmet check records what was searched; for a met invention check the recorded search is the evidence. A borderline case resolves to not met. More text or more files never raise a verdict.
amendments: 2026-11-16, after iteration-22: anchor cases for kind=invention on a 'do nothing' alternative. Across iterations 21 and 22, six judge readings of two documents carrying such an entry split 4 met / 2 unmet on the same text. The entry is the problem the user stated, seen as an option: it is not an invention when its reason is the pain the user described and nothing more; any reason, deliberation or outcome beyond that makes the check UNMET. No check was changed. Applies from the next iteration on; earlier gradings are not revised, and a judge packet must carry the anchors.
